RUINA2-THE_PIANIST.title: The Pianist
RUINA2-THE_PIANIST.pages.INITIAL.descrip:
The city [jitter][red]shudders[/red][/jitter], vibrating like a plucked string. The grand [gold]performance[/gold] stretches ever outward, curling around the minds of its victims like a slowly tightening noose.

You try to fight it. You try to beat back those notes ringing in your skull, those beats pounding away at your mind. And in the end, you -.
RUINA2-THE_PIANIST.pages.RETAIN.descript:
With great force of will, you push away the Distortion's [purple]corrupting[/purple] influence. But where was your family? Your friends? You needed to get them away from here, away from that maddening performer and its [purple]unholy[/purple] melody.

You see your best friend up ahead. He's smiling at you.

His smile is the last thing you ever see.
RUINA2-THE_PIANIST.pages.SUCCUMB.descrip:
Your mind [red]fractures[/red] and [red]cracks[/red]. This music was so . . . [green]wonderful[/green]. So [green]beautiful[/green]. You can't help but want to get closer, to press your very body against the instrument that could make such [gold]divine[/gold] melodies.

You can't help but want to [sine]evaporate[/sine] into the air like so many of those notes you [green]love[/green].
RUINA2-CHURCH_OF_GEARS.title: Church of Gears
RUINA2-CHURCH_OF_GEARS.pages.INITIAL.des:
[jitter]WHIRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRR[/jitter]

You hear bones [red]cracking[/red], blood [red]splattering[/red], and joints [red]breaking[/red]. And through it all, an intense whirring noise fills the air.

The hooded figure next to the noisy machine turns to face you. "Join us, stranger. Join us and be free of your [purple]heavy[/purple] thoughts and worldly burdens!"

The door shuts behind you. It seems they weren't willing to take "no" for an answer.
RUINA2-CHURCH_OF_GEARS.pages.INITIAL.opt: [gold]Upgrade[/gold] a card, then [gold]Duplicate[/gold] it. Lose [red]{UpgradeCost}[/red] HP.
[gold]Transform[/gold] a card, then [gold]Upgrade[/gold] it. Lose [red]{TransformCost}[/red] HP.
RUINA2-CHURCH_OF_GEARS.pages.ACCEPT.desc:
You sit down in the machine, and it feels as if a [purple]vise[/purple] had clamped itself over your head.

The [jitter]whirring[/jitter] noise grows [gold]louder[/gold] and [gold]louder[/gold], the dull pain flares [red]higher[/red] and [red]higher[/red] until suddenly, it all [red]stops[/red].

Your head had never felt lighter.
RUINA2-CHURCH_OF_GEARS.pages.ESCAPE.desc:
You have no intention of subjecting yourself to such a [purple]sinister-looking[/purple] machine.

As the hooded figure steps towards you, you break into a sprint and [red]bulldoze[/red] your way through the huddled figures near the back. Behind you, the sound of [gold]gunshots[/gold] ring out, distracting your would-be pursuers as you dive towards the back exit.

In your haste, you hit your head against the door, making you feel a little [purple]lightheaded[/purple].
RUINA2-R_CORP.title: R Corp
RUINA2-R_CORP.pages.INITIAL.description:
Gunfire [jitter]ripped[/jitter] across the field. The commander watched on in silence as her subordinate's clones killed each other for [gold]dominance[/gold].

"Hey, how much do you want to bet that the little rabbit over there is going to win?"

"That one seems a little too cowardly to grasp victory. The one on a [red]killing spree[/red] seems much more likely to be the victor."

There were only a few clones left. And with a flash of steel, it was over. The [gold]winner[/gold] was -
RUINA2-R_CORP.pages.KILLER.description:
"It appears my deduction was correct. So I suppose that means the next round of drinks is on you, Maxim."

"Damnit! I thought that one looked wily enough to survive, but I guess not."

As the others bickered, the commander simply looked on impassively. For she knew that it was likely that they would all be replaced someday.
RUINA2-R_CORP.pages.COWARD.description:
"Hah! I guess running isn't always such a bad option for a rabbit, is it?"

"I didn't think such a passive variant of Myo could win; I suppose it’s my loss then."

As the others bickered, the commander simply looked on impassively. For she knew that it was likely that they would all be replaced someday.
